newsitem.title: UK: Copper margin move designed to cool market - trade.
newsitem.headline: Copper margin move designed to cool market - trade.

text.p: The doubling of copper spread margins by the London Clearing House (LCH) appears to be a move to cool down a market where stocks are at critically low levels.
On Monday, the LCH raised the cash/three months spread margin to $3,750 per lot of 25 tonnes from $1,875, and lifted extended spread margins to $4,250 from $3,000.
This action should deter fundamental tightness from being further exacerbated by speculative activity, sources said.
"It will help to prevent a speculative accumulation on top," one said.

Currently, LME copper stocks stand at 6-1/4 year lows of just 93,900 tonnes, while the cash/threes backwardation is around $160 a tonne. Back in September, the cash market was at a small contango to three months, while LME inventories were a high 275,775 tonnes.

Since then, stocks have been remorselessly whittled down as copper has flowed out to meet arbitrage demand from China and the U.S., or to meet requirements normally satisfied by scrap and off-grades, as these are also in short supply.
But other traders felt that the speculative heat is already evident in the market, and that the LME's December dates and options were in danger of becoming over-heated.

"It does make you wonder, especially when all these regulators are looking at it. The backwardation limit is still in place, so what are they (the authorities) seeing that we cannot see?" one trader said.

Copper shot higher in recent weeks after a long spell of range-trading between $1,900/2,050. Last week, prices hit $2,240 - the highest since the Sumitomo Corp shake-out in June - and are currently around $2,195.
"They cannot be worried about the longs, so they must be worried about the shorts," the trader said.

Also, with prices motoring higher in November perceptions in the options market have changed, just ahead of December declarations. The emphasis has switched away from downside puts towards upside calls as they get nearer to being "in-the-money'.
Cash copper is now around $2,350/tonne, some way above the levels of a month ago, as both the backwardation and the three months market has risen.
Above the market at the $2,400, $2,500, and $2,600 call strikes option interest is high at 2,145, 2,570 and 6,970 lots respectively.
Upside puts are much smaller, by contrast, while 2,065, 1,259 and 1,528 lots of $2,000, $2,100 and $2,000 strike puts are now out-of-the-money.

Some traders also suggested that the margin move, intended to reduce price volatility, will calm concerns that some companies are facing financial problems or considering leaving the LME ring, as Lehman Brothers Commodities did last week.
